findings.title: Audit section misattributes the delta provider and does not match `compute_delta`'s contract
findings.description:
Line 73 credits **323** with `compute_delta` and `is_within_floor`, and line 326 repeats `compute_delta` under "323: ... unchanged". Both belong to slice **324**: 324's design assigns `audit_delta.py`, `compute_delta(baseline: ProjectBaseline, new_run: AuditRun) -> DeltaReport`, `DeltaCell.within_floor` and `is_within_floor` to itself; 323's design lists `baseline_report`, `AuditRun`, `AuditNoiseFloor`, `FloorStat` and `ProjectBaseline`, and never mentions either function. 324 is absent from the frontmatter `dependencies` and from the slice-plan entry for 403, even though 403 now imports its code (the architecture's "Related Work" sanctions reusing 320's delta, but the providing slice still has to be named).

More consequentially, the Data Flow (line 149: `audit: baseline at before_sha, latest run at after_sha, same prompt hash → compute_delta`) and D8 (line 236: "The baseline is the latest run at `before_sha` and the new run is the latest at `after_sha`") describe feeding two `AuditRun`s. `compute_delta` takes a `ProjectBaseline` plus one `AuditRun`, and `baseline_report(store, *, project_filter=...)` returns every `(project_id, commit_sha, audit_prompt_hash)` group with no commit filter. Nothing in the design says how the `before_sha` group is selected, how that group's `FloorStat`/`floor_n_runs` reaches `is_within_floor` and the `AuditSection`, or what happens when several instruments match. Criterion 8 (line 339) restates the two-run framing. This leaves the slice-plan requirement "LLM-sourced numbers are shown against their noise floor" and the architecture's "before/after deltas are reported against [the floor]" without a specified construction path. Fix: name 324 as the provider, declare the dependency, and specify filtering `baseline_report`'s output to the `before_sha`/prompt-hash `ProjectBaseline` before calling `compute_delta`.

findings.title: Range resolver converts git failures into a benign unresolved result and exit 0
findings.description: The only resolver failure row (line 164) says a reflog read or merge search returning `None` is "treated as 'this path can't answer'", tries the next path, and emits an INFO line per unresolved slice; line 275 then says `slice-ranges` "Exits 0 when every slice either resolved or was unresolved for a stated reason". But `None` covers two different events: a genuine "no merges found" and `run_git` failing to answer (30 s timeout, spawn failure, non-zero return code). The Data Flow (lines 112-114) does `none found → fast-forward landing`, so a timed-out `git log --merges --first-parent` on a large repository is indistinguishable from a real fast-forward: the command prints `unresolved: reflog_unavailable` and exits 0 instead of erroring. The same collapse affects `merge-base`, the containment/first-parent checks and `git cat-file -e` (a git failure there reads as "commit <sha> not found", line 165), and `report history`'s first-parent `git log` ordering (line 298) has no failure row at all. This contradicts the design's own CLI contract ("Exits 1 on a git or store error", line 275) and its rule that "a `None` from `run_git` is never an answer" (line 327, echoing 400's "A `None` (git couldn't answer) is a preflight failure, never treated as a clean tree"). It leaves criterion 1 ("resolves from topology alone ... including in a fresh clone") and criterion 11 unmet whenever git cannot answer. Fix: distinguish `run_git` `None`/non-zero from a legitimate empty search, add a distinct git-error path with ERROR + exit 1, and enumerate hang/timeout/refusal for `git log --first-parent`, `merge-base`, the containment checks and `cat-file -e`.

findings.title: 401's snapshot-compatibility rule is not restated, and 403 may have to edit 401's code
findings.description: 401's design states that snapshot records written by 400 fail its `LanguageSnapshot` every-metric validation and are skipped by the store's tolerant scan, and that "403 reads only snapshots taken by 401 or later (Compatibility)". 403's Prerequisites says 401 is "not a prerequisite" and commits to a conditional ("If 401 is implemented after 403, it inherits the `environment_root` rule ... If before, 403 updates whatever of 401's code reads `ctx.repo_root`"), but 401 is not in `dependencies` and the compatibility rule is never restated. Behavior still works — `ensure_snapshot` re-measures a skipped boundary snapshot — so this does not leave a criterion unmet, but the plan's implementation order puts 401 before 403, which makes "403 updates 401's code" the expected branch of a hidden ordering dependency. Naming the assumed order and the skipped-snapshot behavior would remove the ambiguity between two unimplemented slices.

findings.title: Durable range resolution matches the architecture's attribution rules
findings.description: D2 restricts the merge search to the target's first-parent line, refuses `_find_merge_commit`'s `main` fallback (which can span a batch promotion), confines the slice-number grep to the established merge-message convention, and returns `LANDED_ELSEWHERE` rather than guessing for side-branch landings. D3 uses `M^1 → M` for before/after while retaining `fork_sha`/`tip_sha` for 420's `fork..tip`. This is exactly the architecture's Envisioned State ("the merge commit's first parent against the merge commit ... refined in slice 403, D3, so other work merged after the fork isn't counted") and its Technical Considerations ("Inferring attribution from ordinary commit messages is not [acceptable]"). Dependency direction is correct: 403 reuses and makes public the existing `review/git_utils.py` helpers (which the architecture names as the resolver this component "reuses and makes durable"), shares `slice_merge_grep_pattern` so `sq review code` is unchanged, and writes one coarse `slice_ranges` record per project keyed on `ProjectId` in 320's store with `schema_version` unchanged.

findings.title: Commit export and environment identity match the architecture
findings.description: `git archive` into a `TemporaryDirectory`, no writes into the measured repo's `.git`, rule-set configs and sources from the exported tree, tools/venv from the live checkout through the required `AdapterContext.environment_root`, and the `uv.lock` SHA-256 gate for type counts implement the architecture's "A snapshot measures a commit ... Any other commit is measured from a `git archive` export into a temporary directory, which writes nothing into the measured repository's `.git`", "Measuring an exported commit reads that commit's config, so a config change between two commits shows up as a rule-set change", and "For an exported commit, the current environment is used only when that commit's lockfile matches it; otherwise both metrics are absent with that reason". Coverage at an export is absent (401's stated behavior), dependency installation stays in Future Work, and no new dependencies are added. The `snapshot --commit REV` surface is also endorsed by the architecture's Envisioned State ("The snapshot command ... exports the commit if it isn't a clean HEAD").

findings.title: Breakdown, comparability and noise-floor honesty match the architectural principles
findings.description: D7 diffs only on full measurement identity (metric, language, tool name/version/counting, rule set, environment), names each break, applies `exclusions_changed` to every row and `limits_changed` only to over-limit figures, and never compares across languages. D8 carries n files/functions/review files/findings, the three audit floor states with `n_runs`, marks every review figure `no floor measured` rather than inventing a floor, keeps review severity on its own scale, separates write-time from read-side-mapped counts (402's contract), and shows the `other` share as the architecture's vocabulary-fit evidence. No serialized key contains `score`. This satisfies "Breakdown, not a score", "Absent is not zero", "Normalize categories, not severities", and the plan's criterion "LLM-sourced numbers are shown against their noise floor, and every figure carries its sample size. No composite score appears anywhere". D9's rule that unresolved slices appear at project level only is precisely the architecture's "Slices whose range never resolved roll up at project level only".

findings.title: Export I/O failure modes are enumerated with explicit strategies
findings.description: The table names `rev-parse`/`archive` non-zero or `None`, the `GIT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30 s) hang, extraction `OSError` (disk full, permissions), unknown revision, `data`-filter refusal of absolute paths and links outside the tree, tool hang/failure inside the export (bounded by `metrology.snapshot_tool_timeout_s`), half-a-before-and-after refusal, a stored landing whose commit is gone, concurrent `slice_ranges` writes, and store write failure — each with a named exception (`SnapshotExportError`, `MetrologyStoreError`), a log level, an exit code, temp-directory cleanup on error, and an explicit justification for the one unbounded in-process step. Criterion 11 and the `caplog` assertions in Technical Requirements make them testable; no row says "TBD". The resolver and `report history` git calls are the gap named in the CONCERN above. Note that neither parent architecture document states an NFR with a numeric latency/throughput target, so there is no NFR target to restate; the design does carry forward the applicable bounds (30 s git timeout, `snapshot_tool_timeout_s`, "one store scan per command, not per slice", one write).

findings.title: Scope is proportionate and the exclusions are justified by named reasons
findings.description: The mechanism count fits a 4/5 slice the plan assigns five deliverables (durable ranges, commit export, three reports), and every assigned item is present: topology and reflog resolution, first-time persistence, fresh-clone durability, `git archive` without touching `.git`, the lockfile gate, full-identity comparison, on-demand boundary snapshots, noise-floor/sample-size display, and project-level fallback. Exclusions each carry a reason tied to an architecture non-goal or a plan item: no audits/reviews run from a report, no fabricated review noise floor, no dependency installation (Future Work), no ESLint `node_modules` identity (#250), no composite score/gate/pipeline hook, and no slice table in `report project` ("no success criterion needs it"). D4 justifies the separate `slice-ranges` command concretely (persist the reflog before `git gc` without paying for pyright). I found no section that restates another document at length, no configuration or abstraction with no consumer, and no scope assigned to this slice that was dropped or deferred.

structured_findings.summary: Audit section misattributes the delta provider and does not match `compute_delta`'s contract
Range resolver converts git failures into a benign unresolved result and exit 0
401's snapshot-compatibility rule is not restated, and 403 may have to edit 401's code
Durable range resolution matches the architecture's attribution rules
Commit export and environment identity match the architecture
Breakdown, comparability and noise-floor honesty match the architectural principles
Export I/O failure modes are enumerated with explicit strategies
Scope is proportionate and the exclusions are justified by named reasons
